ruling.recommended_action: Send to human review: decide the scope of the rider's 09:18 general consent and the non-exempt km of the 09:20–09:26 segment (no account action recommended).
ruling.reasoning:
RydeTAXI trip, metered fare $45.04 [F7]; one off-route segment 09:20–09:26 runs 4.04 km where the optimal route covers 1.86 km, +2.18 km, up to 1027 m off route [F3][F1]. The RD-4 branch is settled against the driver: no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch, and a speed band alone does not exempt [F15][F12][RD-4].

The interpretive element the code cannot settle is the RD-5 branch for F3: did the rider's message agree to this route, and does its scope cover the segment? The rider wrote at 09:18, before the segment started at 09:20 [F9][F3]: "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late" [F9], answering the driver's offer "want me to take another way?" [F8]. On its words this is a general route choice, not the naming of any road, so no record could tie the segment to a named road [RD-5][F9][F8]. The driver's own statement frames what he did as getting ahead of the traffic jams — "so I went round" — with no errand, stop or loop of his own [F11][RD-5]; nothing places the segment elsewhere. Whether a general authorisation of this kind covers the whole 4.04 km segment, or only the 1.86 km the optimal route itself would have covered, is not something the record settles: the rider's words are read one way by the driver and another in the complaint, and the timing and traffic facts pull both ways — the ECP band-2 jam ran 08:58–09:20 and was clearing exactly as the segment began [F12][F3], while the trip took 35.4 min against 25.2 min and 21.6 km against 19.3 km [F2][F1].

Because the segment's scope is undetermined and it changes both the amount and the refund outcome, the case cannot be decided here [RD-5][G13] and the ruling is escalate [RD-2][RD-1]. Any eventual refund would be calculated as extra_km × ($30.46 ÷ 21.60 km = $1.4102/km), with the excess billed 2.35 km/$3.31 [F4][F7] not fully refundable because corridor tolerance and matching noise are not [RD-2]; waiting $0.11 is metered waiting and is not refunded [F5][RD-3(c)]. Safety screen: the chat, driver's statement and complaint contain an offer of an alternative route and an apology for lateness, no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. No prior upheld route dispute in 90 days, so RD-6 does not attach [F18][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: Rider message "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late" [F9], sent 09:18, before the segment start 09:20 [F3], is a general route choice answering the driver's offer [F8], and the driver's statement shows no errand of his own [F11] — so the branch is general_route_consent, whose consequence would be exempt. But the record does not settle whether that general authorisation covers the whole 4.04 km / +2.18 km segment or only the 1.86 km the optimal route itself covers [F3][F1]: the jam that justified the substitution was clearing at 09:20 [F12], the trip overran distance and time [F2][F1], and consent scope is a reading of the words that the record leaves open [RD-5][G13]. The segment is therefore undetermined and the case goes to a person; it changes the amount, so it cannot be left undecided [RD-2][RD-1].
